questions.prompt: A fair six - faced dice, with the faces labelled ‘1’, ‘2’, ‘3’, ‘4’, ‘5’, and ‘6’, is rolled thrice. What is the probability of rolling ‘6’ exactly once?
questions.solution:
1. Select which of three rolls shows 6: three choices.
2. For each choice, its probability is (1/6)(5/6)², since both other rolls must avoid 6. The three events are disjoint.
3. Probability=3×(1/6)×25/36=**75/216, A**. Using 25/216 alone would omit the choice of successful roll.

questions.prompt: A square paper, shown in figure (I), is folded along the dotted lines as shown in the figures (II) and (III). Then a few cuts are made as shown in figure (IV). Which one of the following patterns will be obtained when the paper is unfolded? Note: The figures shown are representative. (I) (I I ) (I II ) (I V )
questions.solution:
1. Undo the second diagonal fold by reflecting every cut across that fold line, then undo the first fold by another reflection. A cut on a fold joins its own mirror; an interior cut appears separately in each reflected layer.
2. The triangular boundary cuts point outward at the four sides. The rectangular cuts give square holes at one opposite corner pair and reflected L-shaped pairs at the other.
3. These positions and orientations match **A**. B rotates square holes into diamonds; C reverses triangular directions; D merges distinct interior holes.

questions.prompt: A shop has 4 distinct flavors of ice - cream . One can purchase any number of scoops of any flavor . The order in which the scoops are purchased is inconsequential. If one wants to purchase 3 scoops of ice - cream, i n how many ways can one make th at purchase?
options: 48 Q.1 1 – Q. 3 5 Carry ONE mark Each
questions.solution:
1. Let xi be the number of scoops of flavour i. The purchase is determined by a nonnegative integer solution x1+x2+x3+x4=3.
2. Stars and bars gives binomial(3+4−1,4−1)=binomial(6,3)=20.
3. Hence **B**. Ordering scoops would overcount the same purchase; repetition of a flavour is allowed.

questions.prompt:
Suppose a program is running on a non - pipelined single processor computer system. The computer is connected to an external device that can interrupt the processor asynchronously. The processor needs to execute the interrupt service routine (ISR) to serve this interrupt. The following steps (not necessarily in order) are taken b y the processor when the interrupt arrives: (i) The processor saves the content of the program counter. (ii) The program counter is loaded with the start address of the ISR. (iii) The processor finishes the present instruction. Which ONE of the following is the CORRECT sequence of steps? ( A ) (iii), (i), (ii) ( B ) (i), (iii), (ii)
( C ) (i), (ii), (iii) ( D ) (iii), (ii), (i)
options: Option (A) in the original question below
Option (B) in the original question below
Option (C) in the original question below
Option (D) in the original question below
questions.solution:
1. In the stated nonpipelined model, an asynchronous interrupt is handled after completing the current instruction. That establishes (iii) first.
2. Save the program counter for the interrupted program before overwriting it, then load the ISR’s starting address.
3. The order is **(iii),(i),(ii), A**. Saving after the ISR address is loaded would lose the return location.

questions.prompt: Which ONE of the following statements is FALSE regarding the symbol table?
options: Symbol tabl e is responsible for keeping track of the scope of variables.
Symbol table can be implemented using a binary search tree.
Symbo l table is not required after the parsing phase.
Symbol table is created during the lexical analysis phase.
questions.solution:
1. The symbol table records identifiers, scopes and attributes and can use a search-tree implementation. Entries may begin during lexical analysis and be enriched by later phases.
2. Semantic checks, type checking, intermediate-code generation and later code generation still need information about those symbols.
3. Therefore ‘not required after parsing’ is the false statement, **C**.

questions.prompt: Which ONE of the following techniques used in compiler code optimization uses live variable analysis?
questions.solution:
1. Two variables whose values are simultaneously live cannot safely share the same register. Liveness intervals or an interference graph express these constraints.
2. Register allocation/assignment uses this information to reuse registers for nonoverlapping lifetimes and spill when necessary.
3. Hence **B**. Constant folding and strength reduction rely on different analyses; call management is not the listed allocation optimization.

questions.prompt: Consider a demand paging memory management system with 32 - bit logical address, 20 - bit physical address, and page size of 2048 bytes. Assuming that the memory is byte addressable , what is the maximum number of entries in the page table? 21
questions.solution:
1. Page size 2048=2¹¹ bytes consumes 11 offset bits of the 32-bit logical address.
2. The virtual page number has 32−11=21 bits, allowing 2²¹ virtual pages and hence that many entries in a full per-process page table.
3. Choose **2²¹, A**. Physical address width limits physical frames, not the number of virtual-page entries.

questions.prompt: A schedule of three database transactions T 1 , T 2 , and T 3 is shown . R i ( A ) and W i ( A ) denote read and write of data item A by transaction T i , i = 1 , 2 , 3 . The transaction T 1 aborts at the end. Wh ich other transaction(s) will be required to be rolled back? R 1 ( X ) W 1 ( Y ) R 2 ( X ) R 2 ( Y ) R 3 ( Y ) ABORT ( T 1 )
questions.solution:
1. T1 writes Y without committing. T2 then reads that version of Y, creating a dependency on uncommitted T1.
2. T3 also reads the Y written by T1. When T1 aborts, both transactions have used a value that must be undone.
3. Cascading rollback affects **both T2 and T3, C**. Their reads of X do not remove this dependency.

questions.prompt: g ( . ) is a function from A to B , f ( . ) is a function from B to C , and their composition defined as f ( g ( . ) ) is a mapping from A to C . If f ( . ) and f ( g ( . ) ) ar e onto ( surjective) functions, which ONE of the following is TRUE about the function g ( . ) ?
options: g ( . ) must be an onto (surjective) function.
g ( . ) must be a one - to - one (injective) function.
g ( . ) must be a bijective function, that is, both one - to - one and onto.
g ( . ) is not required to be a one - to - one or onto function.
questions.solution:
1. Let A={0,1}, B={u,v}, C={c}. Set g(0)=g(1)=u and f(u)=f(v)=c. Then f and f∘g are both surjective.

questions.prompt: Let G be any undirected graph with positive edge weights, and T be a minimum spanning tree of G . For any two vertices , u and v , let d 1 ( u , v ) and d 2 ( u , v ) be the shortest distances between u and v in G and T , respectively. W hich ONE of the option s is CORRECT for all possible G , T , u and v ?
options: d 1 ( u , v ) = d 2 ( u , v )
d 1 ( u , v ) ≤ d 2 ( u , v )
d 1 ( u , v ) ≥ d 2 ( u , v )
d 1 ( u , v ) ≠ d 2 ( u , v )
questions.solution:
1. Every path in spanning tree T is also a path in G, because T uses only edges of G.
2. Minimizing over all G paths can therefore produce no greater distance than minimizing over the restricted paths in T: d1(u,v)≤d2(u,v).
3. Equality can occur, for example when G itself is a tree; strict inequality can occur when a useful non-tree edge is absent. Thus **B** is the universal statement.

questions.prompt: T(0)=1 and T(n)=2T(n−1)+n·2ⁿ for n>0. Find its tight asymptotic order.
options: T ( n ) = Θ ( ( log n ) 2 ) n
questions.solution:
1. Divide T(n)=2T(n−1)+n·2ⁿ by 2ⁿ and define U(n)=T(n)/2ⁿ. The recurrence becomes U(n)=U(n−1)+n with U(0)=1.
2. Summing yields U(n)=1+n(n+1)/2=Θ(n²).
3. Therefore **T(n)=Θ(n²2ⁿ), A**.

questions.prompt: Consider the given system of linear equations for variables x and y , where k is a real - valued constant . Which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT? x + ky = 1 kx + y = − 1
options: There is exactly one value of k for which the above system of equations has no solution.
There exist an infinite number of values of k for which the system of equations has no solution.
There exists exactly one value of k for which the system of equations has exactly one so l ution .
There exists exactly one value of k for which the system of equations has an infinite number of solutions.
questions.solution:
1. The coefficient determinant is 1−k². For every k≠±1, it is nonzero and the solution is unique.
2. For k=1 the equations have the same left side but right sides 1 and −1, so no solution exists. For k=−1, the second equation is the negative of the first, giving infinitely many solutions.
3. Exactly one k gives no solution and exactly one gives infinitely many: **A,D**.

questions.prompt: Let X b e a 3 - variable Boolean function that produces output as ‘ 1 ’ when at least two of the input variables are ‘ 1 ’ . Which of the follo wing statement(s) is/are CORRECT , where a , b , c , d , e are Boolean variables?
options: X ( a , b , X ( c , d , e ) ) = X ( X ( a , b , c ) , d , e )
X ( a , b , X ( a , b , c ) ) = X ( a , b , c )
X ( a , b , X ( a , c , d ) ) = ( X ( a , b , a ) AND X ( c , d , c ) )
X ( a , b , c ) = X ( a , X ( a , b , c ) , X ( a , c , c ) )
questions.solution:
1. Write X as the three-input majority function. For B, if a=b both sides equal a; if a≠b majority(a,b,c)=c and both sides equal c. Thus B holds.
2. X(a,c,c)=c. For D, if a=c both sides equal a; otherwise X(a,b,c)=b and the right side is again X(a,b,c). Thus D holds.
3. A fails at (a,b,c,d,e)=(0,0,0,1,1), giving 0 versus 1. C fails at (0,1,1,1), giving 1 versus 0. Select **B,D**.

questions.prompt: The number − 6 can be represented as 1010 in 4 - bit 2’s complement representation. Which of the following is/are CORRECT 2’s complement representation(s) of − 6 ?

1. Widening a two’s-complement integer requires repeating its sign bit. The sign bit of 1010 is 1.
2. Eight-bit sign extension is 11111010=250−256=−6. Sixteen-bit extension is 1111111111111010=65530−65536=−6.
3. Adding only one leading 1 and filling with zeros instead changes the value. Select **B,D**.

questions.prompt: Which of the fo llowing statement(s) is/are TRU E for any binary search tree (BST) having n distinct integers?
options: The maximum length of a path from the root node to any other node is ( n − 1 ) .
An inorder traversal will always produce a sorted sequence of elements.
Finding an element takes O ( log 2 n ) time in the worst case.
Every BST is also a Min - Heap.
questions.solution:
1. A BST with n nodes can be a chain, with maximum possible root-to-node path length n−1 edges. A is the worst-case height bound accepted here.
2. Inorder traversal is sorted because every left-subtree key is smaller and every right-subtree key larger than its root: B.
3. An unbalanced chain needs O(n) worst-case search, not O(log n); the BST rule also does not make each parent the minimum of its children. C,D are false. Select **A,B**.

questions.prompt: A partial data path of a processor is given in the figu re, where RA, RB, and RZ are 32 - bit registers. Which option(s) is/are CORRECT related to arithmetic operations using the data path as shown?
options: The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving two registers.

The data path can only implement arithmetic operations involving one register and one immediate value.

1. Each ALU input has an independent multiplexer selecting a register or an immediate value.

questions.prompt: Suppose in a multiprogramming environment, the following C program segment is executed. A process goes into I/O queue whenever an I/O related operation is performed. Assume that there will always be a context switch whenever a process requests for an I/O , and also whenever the process returns from an I/O . T he number of times the process will enter the ready queue during its lifetime ( not counting the time the process enters the ready queue when it is run initially ) is _______ . questions.prompt: Let S be the set of all ternary strings defined over the alphabet { a , b , c } . questions.prompt: The pseudocode of a function fun() is given below: fun(int A[0,...,n - 1]){ for i=0 to n - 2 for j=0 to n - i - 2 if (A[j]>A[j+1]) then swap A[j] and A[j+1] } Let A [ 0 , ... , 29 ] be an array storing 30 distinct integers in descending order. questions.prompt: A computer has two processors, M 1 and M 2 . Four processes P 1 , P 2 , P 3 , P 4 with CPU bursts of 20, 16, 25, and 10 milliseconds, respectively, arrive at the same time and these are the only processes in the system. The scheduler uses non - preemptive priority scheduling , with priorities decided as follows : • M 1 uses priority of execution for the processes as , P 1 > P 3 > P 2 > P 4 , i.e., P 1 and P 4 have highest and lowest priorities, respectively. • M 2 uses priority of execution for the processes as , P 2 > P 3 > P 4 > P 1 , i.e., P 2 and P 1 have highest and lowest priorities, respectively. A process P i is scheduled to a processor M k , if the processor is free and no other process P j is waiting with higher priority. At any given point of time, a process can be allocated to any one of the free processors without violating the execution priority rules. Ignore the context switch time. What will be the average waiting time of the process es in milliseconds?

questions.prompt: Consider the following two languages over the alphabet { a , b } : + + L 1 = { αβα | α ∈ { a , b } AND β ∈ { a , b } } + + L 2 = { αβα | α ∈ { a } AND β ∈ { a , b } } Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.prompt: In optimal page replacement algorithm, information about all future page references is available to the operating system (OS). questions.prompt: An array A of length n with distinct elements is said to be bitonic if there is an index 1 ≤ i ≤ n such that A [ 1 . . i ] is sorted in the non - decreasing order and A [ i + 1 . . n ] is sorted in the non - increasing order. 2. Search the increasing prefix and decreasing suffix with binary search. A constant number of logarithmic searches is still O(log n), not O(log²n).

questions.prompt: Let F be the set of all functions from { 1 , ... , n } to { 0 , 1 } . Define the binary relation ≼ on F as follows: ∀ f , g ∈ F , f ≼ g if and only if ∀ x ∈ { 1 , ... , n } , f ( x ) ≤ g ( x ) , where 0 ≤ 1 . Which of the following statement ( s ) is /are TRUE?

questions.prompt: Consider a stack data structure into which we can PUSH and POP records. Assume that each record pushed in the stack has a positive integer key and that all keys are distinct. We wish to augment the stack data structure with an O ( 1 ) time MIN operation that returns a pointer to the record with smallest key present in the stack 1) without deleting the corresponding record, and 2) without increasing the complexities of the standard stack operations. Which one or more of the follo wing approach ( es ) can achieve it?

Keep a pointer to the record with the smallest key in the stack.

The contents of the frames are as follows initially and after each reference (from left to right) : initially after - 1* 2* 3* 4* 5* 4 1 6* 4 5 1* 3* 2* - 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 6 6 6 6 6 2 - - 2 2 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 1 1 1 - - - 3 3 5 5 5 5 5 5 5 3 3 The * - mark ed references cause page replacements. questions.prompt: Which of the following Boolean algebra ic equation ( s ) is/are CORRECT ?

questions.prompt: Given a computing system with two levels of cache (L1 and L2) and a main memory. questions.prompt: A 5 - stage instruction pipeline has stage delays of 180, 250, 150, 170, and 250, respectively, in nanoseconds. The delay of an inter - stage latch is 10 nanoseconds. It is compulsory for a student to enroll for exactly 15 credits of core courses and exactly 20 credits of projec t. In addition, a student has to enroll for a minimum of 10 credits of specialization courses . The maximum credits of elective courses that a student can enroll for is ______
questions.solution:
1. To maximize elective credits, use the maximum permitted total, 70, while keeping all other variable requirements at their minimum.
2. Required non-elective credits are 15 core+20 project+10 specialization=45.
3. The remaining 70−45=**25 credits, D** can be electives, satisfying the minimum-total requirement as well.

questions.prompt: ‘When the teacher is in the room, all students stand silently. ’ If the above statement is true, which one of the following statements is not necessarily true?
options: If any student is not standing silently, then the teacher is not in the room.
When the teacher is in the room, all students are silent.
If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room.
When the teacher is in the room, all students are standing.
questions.solution:
1. Write T⇒(standing AND silent). Its contrapositive says a student failing that conjunction implies ¬T, so A follows. B,D each weaken the conjunction and also follow.
2. Observing every student standing does not establish the teacher’s presence: they could stand for another reason or before the teacher arrives.
3. The unsupported converse is **C**.

questions.prompt: Combinatorics deals with problems involving counting. For example, “How many distinct arrangements of N distinct objects in M spaces on a circle are possible?” is a typical problem in combinatorics. This kind of counting is sometimes used in the modeling of several physical pheno mena. Often, in such models, the different combinatorial possibilities are assigned probability values. Assigning probabilities enables the computation of the average values of physical quantities. Consider the following statements: P: Combinatorics is alw ays invoked in the modeling of physical phenomena. Q: Modeling some physical phenomena involves assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities in order to compute average values of physical quantities. Based on the passage above, what can be inferred about statements P and Q?
options: P is False and Q is False
P is False and Q is True
P is True and Q is False
P is True and Q is True
questions.solution:
1. The passage says counting is ‘sometimes’ used in models, not that every physical model invokes combinatorics. P’s universal ‘always’ is not supported.
2. It expressly describes assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities to compute averages in some models, which supports Q.
3. The intended option is **P false, Q true, B**; do not promote a qualified statement into a universal one.

questions.prompt: In the 2020 summer Olympics’ Javelin throw finals, Neeraj Chopra exhibited a spectacular performance to win the gold medal. The s ilver medal was won by Jakub Vadlejch and the b ronze medal was won by Vitezlav Vesely. There were six rounds of throws with each athlete having one throw per round. T he best of all the throws of each athlete is considered for the medal. Following were the observations about the throws : i. The first and second rounds were dominated by Neeraj Chopra with a gold medal performance in his second throw, while the other two athletes did not have any medal winning throws in these rounds . ii. The throws in the last round by both Jakub Vadlejch and Vitezlav Vesely were fouls and were not considered for scoring. iii. After four rounds, Vitezlav Vesely was in the second position and could not improve upon his best throw in the succeeding rounds. iv. In t he fourth round , the throw b y Jakub Vadlejch was the best in that round. In which round did Vitezlav Vesely have his best throw?
questions.solution:
1. Vesely’s best throw occurred by round four, since he could not improve later, and it did not occur in rounds one or two by observation (i). Only rounds three or four remain.
2. If it had occurred in round four, Vadlejch’s best-in-that-round throw would exceed it, placing Vadlejch ahead after four rounds. That contradicts Vesely’s second position then.
3. Vesely’s best must be in the **third round, A**.

questions.prompt: An unbiased six - faced dice whose faces are marked with numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 is rolled twice in succession and the number on the top face is recorded each time. The probability that the number appearing in the second roll is an integer multiple of the number appearing in the first roll is __________
options:
5 6
Q.1 1 – Q. 3 5 Carry ONE mark Each
questions.solution:
1. Count favourable second rolls for each first roll: for 1 there are 6 multiples; for 2 there are 3; for 3 there are 2; for 4,5,6 there is 1 each.
2. Total favourable ordered pairs=6+3+2+1+1+1=14 out of 36 equally likely outcomes.
3. Probability=14/36=**7/18, C**. A number counts as an integer multiple of itself.

questions.prompt: An urn contains one red ball and one blue ball. At each step, a ball is picked uniformly at random from the urn , and this ball together with another ball of the same color is put back in the urn. The probability that there are equal number of red and blue balls after two steps is
questions.solution:
1. After two reinforcement steps, equal colour counts require one red draw and one blue draw, in either order.
2. P(red then blue)=(1/2)(1/3)=1/6 because after drawing red the urn has two red and one blue. By symmetry P(blue then red)=1/6.
3. The disjoint probabilities sum to **1/3, B**.

questions.prompt: Consider 4 × 4 matrices with their elements from { 0 , 1 } . The number of such matrices with even number of 1 s in every row and every column is
questions.solution:
1. Choose the top-left 3×3 binary entries freely: 2⁹ possibilities.
2. Each of the first three rows determines its last entry by even parity; each first-three column similarly determines its bottom entry.
3. The last corner is uniquely determined and satisfies both remaining parities because total row and column parity agree. Count=2⁹=**512, A**.

questions.prompt: For n > 1 , t he maximum multiplicity of any eigenvalue of an n × n matrix with elements from R is

2. The scalar matrix λI attains multiplicity n for its only eigenvalue.
3. Hence the maximum is **n, A**, not n−1 or a larger value.

questions.prompt: Consider a processor P whose in struction set architecture is the load - store architecture. The instruction format is such that the first operand of any instruction is the destination operand. Which one of the following sequences of instructions corresponds to the high - level language stat ement Z = X + Y ? Note : X, Y, and Z are memory operands. R0, R1, and R2 are registers.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following dependencies among the register operands of different instructions can cause a data hazard in a pipelined processor?
questions.solution:
1. In the conventional in-order pipeline assumed here, a later instruction may read an operand before an earlier instruction has written its needed value. That is a read-after-write true dependence.
2. Read-after-read is harmless. WAR and WAW hazards require ordering conditions beyond this ordinary in-order model, such as out-of-order execution or differing write stages.
3. The expected dependence is **RAW, B**.

questions.prompt: With re spect to a TCP connection between a client and a server , w hich one of the following statements is true ?
options: The client and server use a two - way handshake mechanism before the start of data transmission
The server cannot initiate closing of the connection before the client initiates closing of the connectio n
The TCP connection is half - duplex
The client and server can initiate closing of the connection at the same time
questions.solution:

questions.prompt: Let n > 1 . Consider an n × n matrix M with its elements from R . Let the vector n ( 0 , 1 , 0 , 0 , ... , 0 ) ∈ R be in the null space of M . Which of the following options is/are always correct ?
options: There are at least two non - zero vectors in the null space of M
questions.solution:
1. A nonzero vector in M’s null space makes M singular, so det(M)=0: B. Its second column is zero in this case, but other columns may have many possible ranks.
2. Every real scalar multiple of that vector is also in the null space, giving infinitely many nonzero vectors, hence at least two: D.
3. Rank need not be 1 and determinant is not 1. Select **B,D**.

questions.prompt: F(P,Q)=(¬P+Q) XOR (¬P·Q). Which expressions equal F?
questions.solution:
1. Set U=¬P and V=Q. (U+V) XOR (UV) is 1 precisely when exactly one of U,V is 1, so it equals U XOR V.
2. Thus F=¬P XOR Q, the complement of P XOR Q. These are options C and A respectively.
3. Complementing both XOR inputs leaves P XOR Q unchanged, so D is not equivalent; B is its complement. Select **A,C**.

questions.prompt: Consider the 8 - bit signed integers X , Y and Z represented using the sign - magnitude form. The binary representations of X and Y are as follows: X : 1 0110100 Y : 01001100 Which of the following operations to compute Z result(s) in an arithmetic overflow?

questions.prompt: Consider the following grammar where S is the start symbol, and a and b are terminal symbols. S → aSbS ∣ bS ∣ ε Which of the following statements is/are true ?
options: The string abb has two distinct derivations in this grammar
The string abab has only one rightmost derivation
The language generated by the grammar is undecidable
questions.solution:
1. abb has two parse structures: S⇒aSbS can put its extra b in the first S (a(b) b epsilon) or the final S (a epsilon b(b)). Both yield abb with different trees, proving A,B.
2. For abab the first S after initial a must be epsilon (otherwise the required next b would occur too late), and the final S derives ab uniquely. Hence its rightmost derivation is unique: C.
3. Every CFG language is decidable by a membership algorithm such as CYK, so D is false. Select **A,B,C**.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is/are true ?
options: For a grammar to be LL(1), it must be left - recursive
For a grammar to be LL(1), it must be left - factored
The LL(1) parsers are more powerful than the SLR parsers
questions.solution:
1. LL(1) chooses a production deterministically from the nonterminal and one lookahead token, so it does not use backtracking. Left recursion prevents this top-down behaviour rather than enabling it.
2. Common alternative prefixes must be factored so the first-token choice is unambiguous; this is the standard left-factoring requirement in C.
3. SLR parsers recognize a broader grammar class than LL(1), so D is false. Select **C**.

questions.prompt: With respect to deadlocks in an operating system, which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
options: Banker’s algorithm is used to prevent deadlocks
Deadlock formation can be prevented by ensuring that the hold and wait condition is not allowed
An assignment edge in a resource allocation graph is marked from a process to a resource
A safe state guarantees that all processes can finish without formation of a deadlock
questions.solution:
1. Banker’s algorithm avoids unsafe allocations; it is deadlock avoidance rather than prevention, so A is false.
2. Preventing hold-and-wait breaks a necessary deadlock condition, making B true. A safe sequence guarantees an order in which processes can finish: D true.
3. Assignment edges run resource→process; process→resource is a request edge. Thus C is false. Select the false statements **A,C**.

questions.prompt: Let P , Q , R and S be the attributes of a relation in a relational schema. Let X ⟶ Y indicate functional dependency in the context of a relational database , where X , Y ⊆ { P , Q , R , S } . Which of the following options is/are always true ?

questions.prompt: The height of a binary tree is the number of edges in the longest path from the root to a leaf in the tree. The maximum possible height of a full binary tree with 23 nodes is ___ _____ _ . ( answer in integer )

3. A comb-shaped full tree with one continuing child and one leaf at each level attains 23 nodes and height **11**.

questions.prompt:
Consider a system consisting of k instances of a resource R , being shared by 5 processes. Assume that each process requires a maximum of two instances of resource R and a process can request or release only one instance at a time. Further, a process can request the second instance of the resource only after acquiring the first in stance. The minimum value of k for the system to be deadlock - free is ______ __ . ( answer in integer )
6 – 5 Carry TWO marks Each
questions.solution:
1. With five instances, all five processes can each hold one and request a second, leaving no free instance: a reachable deadlock. Smaller supplies cannot guarantee progress either.
2. With six instances, after each process holds at most one, an additional instance remains. At least one requesting process can acquire its second, finish and release both, enabling another to finish.
3. Thus the guaranteed deadlock-free minimum is **6**.

questions.prompt: Consider the following code snippet in C language that computes the number of nodes in a non - empty singly linked list pointed to by the pointer variable head . struct node{ int elt; struct node *next; }; int get ListSize (struct node *head) { if( E1 ) return 1; return E2 ; } Which one of the following options gives the correct replacements for the expressions E1 and E2 ?

questions.prompt: Let G ( V , E ) be an undirected, edge - weighted graph with integer weights . The weight of a path is the sum of the weights of the edges in that path. The length of a path is the number of edges in that path. Let s ∈ V be a vertex in G . For every u ∈ V and for every k ≥ 0 , let d k ( u ) denote the weight of a shortest path (in terms of weight) from s to u of length at most k . If there is no path from s to u of length at most k , then d k ( u ) = ∞ . Consider the statements: S1: For every k ≥ 0 and u ∈ V , d k + 1 ( u ) ≤ d k ( u ) . S2: For every ( u , v ) ∈ E , if ( u , v ) is part of a shortest path (in terms of weight) from s to v , then for every k ≥ 0 , d k ( u ) ≤ d k ( v ) . Which one of the following options is correct ?

Neither S1 nor S2 is true
questions.solution:

2. S2 fails even with positive weights: take edges s–a=1,a–u=1,u–v=1,s–v=10. The global shortest s–v path uses u–v, yet at k=1, dk(u)=infinity and dk(v)=10.
3. The asserted inequality fails. Only S1 is true: **A**.

questions.prompt: A TCP sender successfully establishes a connection with a TCP receiver and starts the transmission of segments. The TCP congestion control mechanism’s slow - start threshold is set to 10000 segments . Assume that the round - trip time is fixed at 1 millisecond. questions.prompt: Consider the implementation of sliding window protocol over a lossless link, with a window size of W frames, where each frame is of size 1000 bits (including header). 3 The bandwidth of the link is 100 kbps (1k = 10 ) and the one - way propagation delay is 100 milliseconds. questions.prompt: f(x)=(|x|/2−x)(x−|x|/2). Which statements are true?

f′ is not differentiable over all the reals

questions.prompt: Let G ( V , E ) be a simple, undirected graph. A vertex cover of G is a subset ′ ′ ′ V ⊆ V such that for every ( u , v ) ∈ E , u ∈ V or v ∈ V . Let the size of the smallest vertex cover in G be k . Let S be any vertex cover of size k . For a vertex v ∈ V , which of the following constraints will always ensure that v ∈ S ?
options: The degree of v is at least k + 1
The vertex v is on a path of length k + 1
The vertex v is on a cycle of length k + 1
The vertex v is a part of a clique of size k
questions.solution:
1. If v is excluded from a vertex cover, all its neighbours must be included to cover every incident edge. Degree at least k+1 would then require more than k cover vertices, impossible for a minimum cover of size k. A forces v into S.
2. Being on a long path or cycle does not force one particular vertex into every minimum cover; alternating covers of an even cycle give counterexamples. Clique membership also allows excluding one chosen clique vertex.
3. Only **A** is guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Let G ( V , E ) be a simple, undirected, edge - weighted graph with unique edge weights. Which of the following statements about the minimum spanning trees (MST) of G is/are true ?
options: In every cycle C of G , the edge with the largest weight in C is not in any MST
In every cycle C of G , the edge with the smallest weight in C is in every MST
For every vertex v ∈ V , the edge with the largest weight incident on v is not in any MST
For every vertex v ∈ V , the edge with the smallest weight incident on v is in every MST

2. Across singleton cut {v}, its unique lightest incident edge belongs to every MST by the cut property: D.
3. A cycle’s lightest edge need not be globally safe: attach a new centre to every vertex of a heavier triangle by still-lighter unique edges, making the centre-star the MST. A vertex’s heaviest edge may be an unavoidable bridge. B,C fail. Select **A,D**.

questions.prompt: Consider the following context - free grammar G . S → abaABAbba A → aaBBAb | bBabaa B → aBb | ab In the above grammar, S is the start symbol, a and b are terminal symbols, and A and B are non - terminal symbols. Let L ( G ) be the language generated by the grammar G . For a string s ∈ L ( G ) , let n 1 ( s ) be the number of a ’s in s and n 2 ( s ) be the number of b ’s in s . Which of the following statements is/are true?
options: There is a string s ∈ L ( G ) such that n 1 ( s ) < n 2 ( s )
For every string s ∈ L ( G ) , n 1 ( s ) ≥ n 2 ( s )
There is a string s ∈ L ( G ) such that n 1 ( s ) > 2 n 2 ( s )
For every string s ∈ L ( G ) , n 1 ( s ) ≤ 2 n 2 ( s )
questions.solution:
1. B derives aⁿbⁿ, so its a/b counts are equal. A’s base bBabaa contributes three a’s and two b’s beyond B; its recursive aaBBAb adds two a’s and one b plus balanced B strings.
2. Inductively every A string has at least as many a’s as b’s and at most twice as many. S’s terminal prefix/suffix together contribute three of each; combining A,B,A preserves both inequalities.

questions.prompt: Consider the following two s yntax - d irected d efinitions SDD 1 and SDD2 for type declarations. The non - terminal V 1 is the same as V and the non - terminal D 1 is the same as D . Here, the subscript is used to differentiate the grammar symbols on the two sides of a production. The function put updates the symbol table wit h the type information for an identifier. Let P and Q be the languages specified by grammars G1 and G2, respectively. Which of the following statements is/are true ?

questions.prompt: Consider a system that has a cache memory unit and a memo ry management unit (MMU). The address input to the cache memory is a physical address. The MMU has a translation lookaside buffer (TLB). Assume that when a page is evicted from the main memory, the corresponding blocks in the cache are marked as invalid. For a given memory reference, which of the following sequences of events can NEVER happen?
options: TLB miss, Page table hit, Cache hit
TLB hit , Page table miss , Cache hit
TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache hit
TLB miss , Page table miss, Cache miss
questions.solution:
1. A valid TLB hit represents a valid resident-page translation. It cannot simultaneously have a page-table miss in this model, so B is impossible.
2. A page-table miss means the page is absent. The question invalidates its corresponding physical cache blocks on eviction, so a cache hit for that missing page cannot occur: C impossible.
3. A TLB miss can coexist with a resident page and cache hit (A), and a page fault leads to a cache miss (D). Select **B,C**.

questions.prompt: An undirected, unweighted , simple graph G ( V , E ) is said to be 2 - colorable if there exists a function c : V → { 0 , 1 } such that for every ( u , v ) ∈ E , c ( u ) ≠ c ( v ) . Which of the following statements about 2 - colorable graphs is/are true ?

If G is 2 - colorable, then G may contain cycles of even length
An optimal algorithm for testing whether G is 2 - colorable runs in time Θ ( | V | + | E | ) , if G is represented as an adjacency list
An optimal algorithm for testing whether G is 2 - colorable runs in time Θ ( | E | log | V | ) , if G is represented as an adjacency list
questions.solution:

2. BFS/DFS assigns opposite colours along each edge and checks conflicts, touching each vertex and adjacency-list edge a constant number of times: Θ(|V|+|E|). C is true.
3. The added logarithmic factor in D is unnecessary and is not the optimal bound. Select **B,C**.

questions.prompt: The EX stage of a pipelined processor performs the memory read operations for LOAD instructions, and the operations for the arithmetic and logic instructions. Let t EX denote the time taken by the EX stage to perform the operation for an instruction. For each instruction type, the values of t EX and M (the number of instructions of that type in a sequence of 100 instructions for a program P), are given in the table below . The durati on of the pipeline clock cycle is 1 nanosecond. Assume that the latch time for the interstage buffers in the pipeline is negligible. Instruction t EX in M nanoseconds LOAD 1.8 15 IMUL 1.5 10 IDIV 2.5 5 FADD 1.7 10 FSUB 1.7 5 FMUL 2.8 15 FDIV 3.2 5 All other Less than 35 instructions 1.0 When program P is executed, the number of clock cycles for which the pipeline is stalled due to structural hazards in the EX stage is ______. questions.prompt: Consider a table T , where the elements T [ i ] [ j ] , 0 ≤ i , j ≤ n , represent the cost of the optimal solutions of different subproblems of a problem that is being solved using a dynamic programming algorithm. The recursive formulation to compute the table entries is as follows: T [ 0 ] [ k ] = T [ k ] [ 0 ] = 1 for k = 0 , 1 , 2 , ... , n T [ i ] [ j ] = 2 T [ i − 1 ] [ j ] + 3 T [ i ] [ j − 1 ] for 1 ≤ i , j ≤ n Consider the following two algorithms to compute entries of T . Assume that for both the algorithms, for all 0 ≤ i , j ≤ n , T [ i ] [ j ] has been initialized to 1. Algorithm B 1 : For i = 1 , 2 , ... , n For j = 1 , 2 , ... , n T [ i ] [ j ] = 2 T [ i − 1 ] [ j ] + 3 T [ i ] [ j − 1 ] Algorithm B 2 : For s = 2 , 3 , ... , 2 n For i = 1 , 2 , ... , n For j = 1 , 2 , ... , n If ( i + j = = s ) T [ i ] [ j ] = 2 T [ i − 1 ] [ j ] + 3 T [ i ] [ j − 1 ] A lgorithm B k , k ∈ { 1 , 2 } is said to be correct if and only if it calculates the correct value s of T [ i ] [ j ] , for all 0 ≤ i , j ≤ n , (as per the recursive formulation) at the end of the execution of the algorithm B k . Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Both algorithms B 1 and B 2 are correct
Algorithm B 1 is correct, but algorithm B 2 is incorrect
Algorithm B 2 is correct, but algorithm B 1 is incorrect
Both algorithms B 1 and B 2 are incorrect
questions.solution:
1. Every T[i][j] depends only on T[i−1][j] and T[i][j−1]. Row-major B1 has completed the prior row and current row’s preceding column, so it respects both dependencies.
2. In B2, both predecessors have coordinate sum s−1 and were completed in the previous diagonal iteration, so it also respects dependencies.
3. Both are correct: **A**. Their costs differ: B1 is Θ(n²), while the written triple-loop B2 is Θ(n³) despite only Θ(n²) updates.

questions.prompt: In the context of schema normalization in relational DBMS, consider a set F of functional dependencies. The set of all functional dependencies implied by F is called the closure of F. To comp ute the closure of F, Armstrong’ s Axioms can be applied. Consider X , Y , and Z as sets of attributes over a relational schem a. The three rules of Armstr ong’ s Axioms are described as follows. Reflexivity : If Y ⊆ X , then X → Y Augmentation : If X → Y , then XZ → YZ for any Z Transitivity : If X → Y and Y → Z , then X → Z T he additional rule of Union is defined as follows. Union: If X → Y and X → Z , then X → YZ It can be proved that the additional rule of Union is also implied by the three rules of Arms trong’s Axioms. L isted below are four combinations of these three rules. Which one of the se combinations is both necessary and sufficient for the proof ?
questions.solution:
1. From X→Y, augment with X to obtain X→XY (since XX=X). From X→Z, augment with Y to obtain XY→YZ.
2. Transitivity then gives X→YZ, proving union without any use of reflexivity.
3. Augmentation alone does not combine the two independent consequences, and transitivity alone cannot add the required attributes to both sides. The necessary sufficient combination among the options is **augmentation and transitivity, D**.

questions.prompt: Consider the transmission of data bits 110001011 over a link that uses Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) code for error detection. If the generator bit pattern is given to be 1001, which one of the following options shows the remainder bit pattern appended to the data bits before transmission ?
questions.solution:
1. Generator 1001 has degree 3, so append three zero bits to data 110001011, obtaining 110001011000.
2. Divide in GF(2), using XOR for subtraction. Cancelling leading terms in turn gives 010101011000, 000111011000, 000011111000, 000001101000, 000000100000, and 000000000100.
3. The last three bits are **100, D**. Appending that remainder to the original data produces a codeword divisible by 1001 with zero remainder.

questions.prompt: 4 Consider a processor that has 16 general purpose registers and it uses 2 - byte instruction format for all its instructions. Variable - sized opcodes are permitted. questions.prompt: An index in a DBMS is said to be dense if an index entry appears for every 6 search - key value in the indexed file. Otherwise it is called a sparse index. Consid er the following two statements. S1: A h ash index must be a dense index + S2: A B t ree index can be a sparse index Which one of the following options is correct?

Both S1 and S2 are false

questions.prompt: 7 Consider the following two finite automata D 1 and D 2 . Which of the following statements is/are true?

∗ ( L ( D 1 ) ∪ L ( D 2 ) ) consists of all strings in { 0 , 1 } whose length is divisible by 3

questions.prompt: 8 i j k l Let Σ = { a , b , c , d } and let L = { a b c d ∣ i , j , k , l ≥ 0 } . Which of the following constraints ensure(s) that the language L is context - free?

questions.prompt: Consider a binary search tree (BST) with n leaf nodes ( n > 0 ). Given any node V , the key present in the node is denoted as Val ( V ) . All the keys present in the given BST are distinct. The k eys belong to the set of real numbers. For a node V , let Suc ( V ) denote the node that is its inorder successor. If a node V does not have an inorder successor , then Suc ( V ) is NULL . As there are no duplicates , if Suc ( V ) is no t NULL , t hen Val ( V ) < Val ( Suc ( V ) ) . Cor responding to every leaf node L i that has a non - NULL Suc ( L i ) , a new key k i with the following property is to be inserted into the BST. Val ( L i ) < k i < Val ( Suc ( L i ) ) Let K represent the list of all such new keys to be inserted into the BST. Which of the following statements is/ are true ?
options: K will have at least one element
After inserting all keys from K , the height of the BST can increase at most by one
Number of nodes in the BST will double after inserting all keys from K
questions.solution:
1. Every new key lies strictly between an original leaf and its original inorder successor. Such open gaps for distinct leaves are disjoint, so inserted keys cannot duplicate: A.
2. Searching for such a key follows the old path to that leaf and attaches as its right child. Different gaps do not create deeper chains, so height increases by at most one: C.
3. A one-node tree has no successor for its only leaf, making K empty. Thus B is not guaranteed; adding at most one key per leaf does not generally double all nodes, so D is false. Select **A,C**.

questions.prompt: 1 Consider three processes P1, P2, and P3 running identical code, as shown in the pseudocode below. A and B are two binary semaphores initialized to 1 and 0 , respectively. X is a shared variable initialized to 0. Each line in the pseudocode is executed atomically. Pseudocode of P1, P2, and P3 Wait
options: Option (A) in the original question below
Option (B) in the original question below
Option (C) in the original question below

questions.prompt: 2 Consider a system with a processor and a 4 KB direct mapped cache with block size of 16 bytes. The system has a 16 MB physical memory. Every access to R results in a cache hit

questions.prompt: 7 A non - pipelined instruction execution unit that operates at 1.6 GHz clock takes an average of 5 clock cycles to complete the execution of an instruction. To improve the performance, the system was pipelined with a goal of achieving an average throughput of one instruction per clock cycle. questions.prompt: 1 Consider the following ANSI - C functio n. int func(int start, int end){ int length=end+1 - start; if((length<1)||(start<0)||(end<0)){ return(0); } if(length%3==0){ return(func(start+1, end)); } else if(length%3==1){ return(1+func(start, end - 1)); } else { return(func(start+2, end)); } } The maximum possible value that can be returned from this function is ____________.
